reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Scriver's OMMBID
clinicalPearls: Occupies the intermediate position on the mucopolysaccharidosis type I continuum between severe Hurler and mild Scheie syndromes, reflecting intermediate residual alpha-L-iduronidase activity
Somatic features such as coarse facies, joint stiffness, and dysostosis multiplex are present but cognition is usually preserved or only mildly affected
Corneal clouding, cardiac valve disease, and hepatosplenomegaly develop progressively
Onset of symptoms is typically in mid-childhood, later than classic Hurler syndrome
Recurrent upper airway obstruction, hearing loss, and obstructive sleep apnoea are common management challenges
Diagnosis combines deficient alpha-L-iduronidase activity with elevated urinary dermatan and heparan sulfate
IDUA genotyping helps predict disease severity and guide therapy decisions
reference.pathophysiology: Hurler-Scheie syndrome results from biallelic IDUA variants that leave an intermediate level of residual alpha-L-iduronidase activity, producing a phenotype between the severe and attenuated poles of mucopolysaccharidosis type I. Deficient enzyme activity impairs the stepwise degradation of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate, causing lysosomal accumulation of these glycosaminoglycans throughout connective tissue, cartilage, cornea, heart valves, meninges, and viscera. Progressive substrate storage produces the characteristic multisystem somatic disease, while the greater residual activity compared with Hurler syndrome largely spares the central nervous system. Excess glycosaminoglycan is excreted in the urine. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Hurler syndrome and Scheie syndrome at the extremes of the same spectrum
Other storage disorders with coarse facies and organomegaly
additionalInvestigations: Quantitative and qualitative urinary glycosaminoglycan analysis
IDUA gene sequencing for genotype-phenotype correlation
Echocardiography for valvular and myocardial assessment
Skeletal survey to document dysostosis multiplex
Audiology, ophthalmology, and sleep studies for airway and sensory involvement
redFlags: Progressive airway obstruction or obstructive sleep apnoea
Cervical cord compression from atlantoaxial instability or dural thickening
reference.prognosis: Survival into adulthood is common, but progressive cardiorespiratory, skeletal, and ocular disease causes significant disability. Enzyme replacement therapy can improve somatic manifestations, though it does not cross the blood-brain barrier or reverse established corneal and skeletal changes.
pitfalls: Misclassifying the intermediate phenotype as classic Hurler or mild Scheie, altering prognostic counselling
Underestimating airway risk during anaesthesia in patients with a difficult airway
Failing to monitor for atlantoaxial instability before procedures
Assuming preserved intellect rules out a mucopolysaccharidosis
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
